name: InToolz
description: InToolz is a management tool for Microsoft Intune designed to simplify cross-tenant migrations and bulk configuration tasks. It enables tenant-to-tenant copy of Intune content, bulk assignment deployment and removal between groups, profiles, and applications, and mass updates to description fields. Note that the project is a work in progress, with several features planned for future releases.
keywords: how to copy intune apps between tenants
transfer intune profiles to new tenant
author: Jørgen Sundet

securityCheck.aiSummary: Broad Graph permissions requested by DestinationUserAuthentication imply a large privilege surface. No evidence of obfuscated code, remote code execution, credential theft, data exfiltration, or other malicious execution in the provided snippets. Recommend least-privilege review, careful consent management, and monitoring of token usage to mitigate risk.

noMaliciousPatterns.reason: The code declares a broad set of Microsoft Graph and Device Management scopes (DefaultScopes), including Directory.Read.All, AuditLog.Read.All, Reports.Read.All, RoleManagement.Read.All, DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All, DeviceManagementCloudCA.ReadWrite.All, DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All, DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All, DeviceManagementRBAC.ReadWrite.All, DeviceManagementScripts.ReadWrite.All, DeviceManagementServiceConfig.ReadWrite.All, Group.ReadWrite.All, etc. While these permissions may be legitimate for an Intune admin tool, they create a large access surface and raise risk if credentials are compromised or misused. Recommend applying the principle of least privilege, requesting only necessary scopes, and auditing consent and token usage. Consider using more granular permissions, short-lived tokens, and separating privileges where possible.
